hero.title: Dirty truth or dare, the version that holds nothing back
hero.description: 140 cards for two, spicy or hot, on a single phone and with nothing to prepare.

section1.title: Two levels, because not everyone starts from the same place
section1.p1: A dirty truth or dare that starts too strong does not work: the first dare makes someone uncomfortable and the game ends before it began. That is why this one has two separate levels rather than a single deck.
section1.p2: The spicy mood stays suggestive: questions that make you blush, dares that bring you closer, nothing that forces anyone to undress. The hot mood drops the precautions, the cards are direct and they assume you both know where you are going.
section1.p3: Start with the first even if you think you can skip a step. The laughter of the early cards does more for the rest of the evening than any dare thrown in cold.

section2.title: How it is played
section2.intro: The rules are the same as the classic version, with one extra point that matters more here.
section2.regle1Texte: Spicy or hot. The game never mixes the two decks: what you choose at the start is what you get for the whole game.
section2.regle2Titre: One card at a time, drawn at random
section2.regle2Texte: Truth or dare, you do not choose. You never see the next card, which makes it impossible to prepare an answer or anticipate a dare.
section2.regle3Titre: Passing is built into the game
section2.regle3Texte: Turning a card down brings a forfeit, and that is all. It is the most important rule in this version: it makes refusing ordinary instead of an admission.
section2.regle4Titre: You set the limit, not the game
section2.regle4Texte: Decide before you start what is off the table tonight. A game never replaces an agreement between the two of you, it only makes suggestions.

section3.title: Consent, said simply
section3.p1: This game suggests, it imposes nothing. Every card can be refused without explanation, as many times as needed, and a forfeit is never a punishment to endure. If one of you is not in the mood, the right answer is to stop the game, not to negotiate.
section3.p2: The cards are written for a couple playing together, between consenting adults. They assume you know each other and that you both know when to stop.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: How is it different from the classic version?
faq.a1: The cards. The classic version is for every couple and can be played in front of anyone. This one has its own decks, spicy and hot, written for a moment when it is just the two of you.
faq.a2: The spicy mood stays suggestive and never asks anyone to undress completely. The hot mood is noticeably more direct, with cards that assume an intimacy already in place. You pick the level before you start.
faq.a3: 140 across the two levels, between truths, dares and forfeits. They do not repeat until the deck runs out, which is enough for several evenings without landing on the same ones.
faq.q4: Is it suitable for a couple who have just met?
faq.a4: The spicy mood, yes, it works well for testing the water. The hot mood assumes you already know each other well: started too early, it makes people uncomfortable rather than entertained.
faq.a5: No, and nothing is recorded. The game runs in your browser, your answers never leave the device and there is no game history.

section4.title: What a game like this can really do
section4.p1: It is not going to transform your intimate life, and nobody should ask it to. What it does well is give a frame to a conversation many couples have never really had, because the card asks the question for you.
section4.p2: The rest is yours to decide, and that is exactly as it should be.
